main_text.p: ¶[?]. Ex Hebræorum appellatione, quales erāt quotquot sive Heberi[?], sive Abrahæ posteri, etiā extrà Judeæ fines alibi terrarum agéres. Nec hac se nomenclatione excidere ullā ratione passi essent. Nec minus dicti Hebræi, quæ hodieque procul à Palæstinæ finibus, quique vix aliâ se appellatione insignire solent. Ipse Paulus patriâ quanquam Cilix, civitate Romanus, nihilominus se Hebræum dicit aliquoties, Hebræum ex Hebræis 1.Cor.xi.22. Phil.iii.5. Adeòque solos Palæstinos distinctè à Judæis aliis per provincias dispersos, Hebræos dictos, gratis viri magni, affirmarunt. Quare verò Paulus Hebræis potius quàm Iudæis inscripserit, ratio gemina, 1. quia cómune nomen fuit totius gentis 11. quia Iudæi dicebantur qui tales non tantùm gente sed & religione, unde Ἰουδαΐζειν, Ἰουδαϊσμὸς, ut pluribus Illustris Salmasius de Hellenist. Quæst. v. At Epistola fidelibus & Christianis ex illâ gente inscripta. iii. Idé colligimus ex occasione Epistolæ, quæ communis Judæis omnibus conversis ad Christi fidé, scripta nempe iis partim in doctrinâ de Messiâ & adimplectione legis confirmandis, partim afflictis tem-

page.notes: The section mark at the start of the first line is a small ornament, transcribed as ¶[?]. The Greek words are copied as far as they can be read; the final letters of Ἰουδαϊσμὸς are uncertain. "Heberi" may be a misprint for "Hebræi"; kept as printed. The printed "signire" is kept as printed. Heading-like text: none.
